summary:
We built SkyBlink: a high-performance, zero-install, open-source web application and astronomical data pipeline engineered for
NASA's upcoming SPHEREx space observatory. SkyBlink ingests calibrated multi-epoch near-infrared FITS datacubes (0.75–5.0 µm),
performs automated World Coordinate System (WCS) tangent-plane reprojection, computes instant difference images (∆I), executes
robust σ-clipping statistical transient candidate detection, locks real-source centroids with an interactive 5× magnification loupe, and
renders instantaneous 102-band pixel spectra for citizen and professional discovery.
details: SPHEREx surveys the entire sky every six months across 102 spectroscopic bands, yielding multi-extension FITS images where wavelength varies across the detector plane. Standard desktop tools (like DS9 or TOPCAT) require complex installations, command-line syntax, and manual coordinate reprojection. This steep technical barrier shuts out citizen scientists, classrooms, and amateur astronomers, leaving vast amounts of temporal infrared data uninspected. As a consequence, faint moving Solar System bodies, cold sub-stellar brown dwarfs, and rapid variable stars risk remaining hidden inside massive raw archives.
